profile_obligation: This file is the baseline-catalogue profile: a single synchronized sweep of six pinned classical corpora across every row of one catalogued source, run once and kept in sync with that source's row set. It is a completeness artifact for that catalogue and nothing more. It is NOT a standing per-row obligation: a new source, result, landscape entry, or conjecture does not inherit a six-corpus sweep, and no row is blocked on one. The obligation that does apply to new work is the novelty-check profile below, which attaches to a claim rather than to a row.
novelty_check_obligation: Required whenever the repository asserts that no formalization or no proof of something exists — in a conjecture's prior_art, a task that calls a target greenfield, or a note claiming a result is unformalized. Such a claim must record what was searched, at which revision, on what date, and what the search did not cover. A claim of absence with no recorded search is not a claim this repository makes.
method: Case-insensitive Unicode-normalized token and phrase search over pinned source snapshots. Hits are candidates, not verified formalizations; per-query counts expose noisy terms, and zero hits are scoped negative evidence only.

novelty_checks.claim: Mathlib carries no o-minimal structures, definable families, or infinite-domain VC theory; its only VC-dimension content is finite and combinatorial.
novelty_checks.method: Filename glob and case-insensitive content grep over the pinned Mathlib source tree for o-minimal, VCDim, Vapnik, and shatter.
novelty_checks.found: Mathlib/Combinatorics/SetFamily/Shatter.lean only: Shatters, shatterer, and a Finset-valued vcDim. No other match.
novelty_checks.scope_limits: One corpus at one revision. Says nothing about third-party Lean packages, other provers, or the wider literature, where o-minimality is of course extensively developed on paper.

novelty_checks.claim: No machine-checked formalization of Breuer's self-measurement propositions exists in the pinned Mathlib or AFP trees.
novelty_checks.method: Case-insensitive recursive content grep over both pinned trees for Breuer and self-measurement.
novelty_checks.scope_limits: Two corpora at their pinned revisions. Rocq/Coq, HOL4, HOL Light and Agda were NOT searched at revision for this claim; a general web search on the same date also surfaced nothing, but that is not a pinned corpus and is not durable evidence. Says nothing about unindexed third-party developments.

novelty_checks.claim: No machine-checked formalization of the Brandenburger-Keisler belief impossibility theorem exists in the pinned Mathlib or AFP trees.
novelty_checks.method: Case-insensitive recursive content grep over both pinned trees for Brandenburger and Keisler.
novelty_checks.found: No match for Brandenburger. Four AFP files match Keisler, all citing Chang and Keisler, Model Theory (Epistemic_Logic and Synthetic_Completeness maximal-consistent-set developments, plus two bibliographies). None concerns the belief impossibility theorem.
novelty_checks.scope_limits: Two corpora at their pinned revisions. Rocq/Coq, HOL4, HOL Light and Agda were NOT searched at revision for this claim. The negative rests on author-name matching, which would miss a formalization that names neither author.

novelty_checks.claim: No machine-checked formalization of the Abramsky-Zvesper categorical reduction of Brandenburger-Keisler exists in the pinned Mathlib or AFP trees.
novelty_checks.method: Case-insensitive recursive content grep over both pinned trees for Zvesper and Abramsky.
novelty_checks.scope_limits: Two corpora at their pinned revisions. Rocq/Coq, HOL4, HOL Light and Agda were NOT searched at revision for this claim. Author-name matching only.

novelty_checks.claim: CORRECTION. An earlier sweep note recorded that no usable categorical formalization of Lawvere's fixed-point theorem was available. That claim was wrong for the AFP.
novelty_checks.method: Case-insensitive recursive content grep over both pinned trees for lawvere.
novelty_checks.found: AFP entry Category_Set (The Elementary Theory of the Category of Sets) carries Fixed_Points.thy with lemma Lawveres_fixed_point_theorem, stated for a point-surjective p : X -> A^X over ETCS cfunc/cset with exponential objects, following Halvorson Theorem 2.6.13, and used there to derive Cantor. This is a genuinely categorical rendering in a maintained, licensed, pinned corpus. Mathlib matches are Lawvere-Tierney topologies in Sites/Grothendieck.lean, a passing mention of Lawvere theories in Subobject/Types.lean, and the Type-level exists_fixed_point_of_surjective in Logic/Function/Basic.lean.
novelty_checks.scope_limits: ETCS is one axiomatized category of sets, not an arbitrary cartesian closed category, so this does not formalize the CCC statement in full generality; it is nonetheless far closer than the Type-level instance and is not, as previously written, unavailable. It is Isabelle/HOL, so it remains true that Lean supplies no categorical version. The earlier negative was reached by web search rather than by grepping this corpus at its pinned revision, which is exactly the failure this record type exists to prevent.

novelty_checks.claim: The pinned Mathlib carries no Shannon entropy of a random variable, and hence no conditional entropy or mutual information. This is a statement about Mathlib and NOT about Lean: conditional Shannon entropy does exist in Lean 4, in the PFR project.
novelty_checks.method: Case-insensitive path glob for entropy across the pinned Mathlib tree, plus symbol grep for measureEntropy, condEntropy and mutualInfo across every package under .lake/packages.
novelty_checks.found: In Mathlib: Dynamics/TopologicalEntropy (Bowen-Dinaburg entropy of a map on a space, a different object), Analysis/SpecialFunctions/BinaryEntropy (the real function h(p)), InformationTheory/KullbackLeibler (Basic and ChainRule), InformationTheory/Hamming and Coding. No Shannon entropy of a random variable, so no conditional entropy. No match for measureEntropy, condEntropy or mutualInfo in any locally pinned package. OUTSIDE Mathlib the picture differs: the PFR project (github.com/teorth/pfr, Apache-2.0, last push 2026-07-25) carries PFR/ForMathlib/Entropy with Basic, Measure, Kernel, Group and RuzsaDist, developing Shannon entropy, conditional entropy H[X|Y] and probability-kernel entropy, with a stated intent to port to Mathlib.
novelty_checks.scope_limits: One corpus at one revision for the negative, plus a web-level check for the positive. PFR pinned leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0-rc1 against the atlas v4.31.0 when this was written, so it was a Path-A reproduction candidate rather than a dependency; as of 2026-08-31 the atlas is on v4.33.0 and PFR is a pinned dependency, though pulling it for entropy alone would still import a very large tree. Not attempted, and no atlas theorem currently needs it: the counting layer LAND-AMBIG-001 covers what is needed without committing to a distribution.

novelty_checks.claim: Time-indexed knowability as developed in AISafetyAtlas.Knowledge.Temporal is NOT novel: it is a measure-free, Sort-polymorphic shadow of Mathlib's filtration and adapted-process theory. No priority is claimed for separating evidence time from target time. What the module has that a filtration does not is that it requires no measurable structure, and that cumulativity is stated as Determines rather than sigma-algebra inclusion because the evidence types at different times are different types.
novelty_checks.method: Directory listing of Mathlib/Probability/Process across the pinned revision, then symbol grep for 'structure Filtration' and 'def Adapted' to read the definitions directly.
novelty_checks.found: Mathlib/Probability/Process/Filtration.lean defines structure Filtration {Omega} (iota) [Preorder iota] (m : MeasurableSpace Omega) with seq : iota -> MeasurableSpace Omega and mono' : Monotone seq - the same preorder-indexed monotone-information shape as EvidenceMonotone. Adapted.lean defines Adapted (f : Filtration iota m) (u : (i : iota) -> Omega -> beta i), which is the family-of-observations form and corresponds to KnowableAt holding at every time. Predictable.lean covers knowability from strictly earlier evidence, Stopping.lean stopping times, PartitionFiltration.lean the partition presentation. The correspondence in the module docstring is by inspection; no formal bridge between the two developments is proved or attempted.
novelty_checks.scope_limits: One corpus at one pinned revision. The correspondence is asserted at the level of definitions read side by side, not established by a Lean theorem, so it is a prior-art pointer rather than an equivalence result. No search was made for filtration-style developments outside Mathlib, and none was made for the specific composite DelayedKnowable, which names a situation rather than proving a theorem.

novelty_checks.claim: Mathlib carries no causal-model machinery: no Bayesian or causal networks, no intervention or do-operator, and no directed reachability or decidable transitive closure that AISafetyAtlas.Causal.Model could have reused instead of defining `ancestors`.
novelty_checks.method: Content grep over the pinned Mathlib source tree for 'bayesian network', 'do-calculus', 'causal model', 'd-separation'; for ReflTransGen together with any Decidable instance; for a Finset-level closure under a step function; and inspection of Mathlib/Combinatorics/Digraph/Basic.lean and SimpleGraph/Connectivity.
novelty_checks.found: No match for any causal term anywhere in the dependency tree, including PFR and Foundation. `Relation.ReflTransGen` exists with no Decidable instance. `Digraph` is a bare adjacency structure with lattice operations only: no walks, no reachability, no acyclicity. `SimpleGraph.Reachable` is undirected and so does not apply. No Finset-level closure operator. One genuine near-miss: `OrderHom.lfp` (Knaster-Tarski, Mathlib/Order/FixedPoints.lean) is the abstract form of `ancestors`, whose defining property is exactly `le_lfp`/`lfp_le`; it is not used because it is built from `sInf` over a set and so does not compute, while the whole purpose of `ancestors` is that (M5) be decidable on a concrete model.
novelty_checks.scope_limits: One corpus at one revision, plus an unpinned web sweep whose results are recorded here as context rather than as corpus evidence. Outside the pinned corpora, two adjacent developments exist and neither supplies what this layer needs: infotheo (Rocq/MathComp, Affeldt et al.) formalizes the graphoid axioms and conditional independence over finite probability mass functions, and Sargsyan's Cubical Agda development (arXiv:2606.20351) formalizes conditional independence, Bayesian conditioning and d-separation soundness. Both target conditional independence; neither defines interventions, a decision variable, a utility, or behavioral equivalence of models, which is the entire content of the layer here. Says nothing about unpinned third-party Lean packages.

novelty_checks.claim: The six baseline formalization corpora plus the pinned CausalForge follow-up contain no reusable layer combining MAIS-A2 finite causal policies, arbitrary local state-map mixtures, interventional utility, regret-bounded policy families, identified sets, model error, and radius predicates.
novelty_checks.method: Case-insensitive content and path search over the six pinned baseline snapshots for decision theory, stochastic policy, utility, regret, identified set, minimax, causal intervention, and interventional value terms, followed by a tracked-source search and manual review of CausalForge Causalean SCM/SWIG/intervention candidates and CausalSmith policy-regret candidates.
novelty_checks.found: No candidate combines the required layer. The baseline corpora contain isolated probability, game-theory, and optimization material. Causalean contains reusable measure-theoretic causal infrastructure, and CausalSmith contains separate observed-law statistical policy-regret and minimax work; neither combines arbitrary local state-map intervention mixtures with the RE24 CID utility/policy-oracle behavior and A2 causal-world-model identified-set/error/radius packaging.
novelty_checks.scope_limits: Seven pinned snapshots are covered: the six baseline corpora and one third-party CausalForge follow-up. This is scoped negative evidence for the combined layer, not a claim that the corpora lack isolated causal, policy, utility, regret, optimization, or minimax definitions. Keyword misses do not prove absence; no CausalForge build reproduction or adapter was attempted, and the check says nothing about other unpinned packages or unpublished developments.

followup_searches.scope: Causalean and CausalSmith Lean sources plus checked-in library metadata
followup_searches.review: Causalean supplies measure-theoretic SCM and SWIG structures, hard fixSet interventions, joint and observational kernels, do-calculus, and identification. CausalSmith supplies separate observed-law statistical policy, welfare-regret, margin/overlap, and minimax developments. Reviewed candidates did not combine arbitrary local state-map mixtures with a CID utility and policy-oracle layer or A2 identified-set, model-error, and radius packaging over causal world models.
followup_searches.scope_limits: One third-party Lean repository at one revision. Keyword misses do not prove absence. The checked-in library index names an older commit and Lean toolchain than the checkout, so the search used the pinned tracked source tree and treats index results as orientation only. CausalForge pins Lean 4.33.0; the atlas pinned 4.31.0 when this was written and moved to 4.33.0 on 2026-08-31, so the toolchain gap recorded here is closed. No build reproduction or adapter was attempted, then or since.
